reasons.C: Closest movement: short aphoristic declaratives cut against longer semicoloned sentences, rhetorical indignation, exclamation used sparingly, and period diction (to-day, some one) without much overdoing it.
reasons.A: Short punchy sentences and an exclamatory aside echo the passage's rhythm, but the tone is gentler and more whimsically confiding (attic, hats) than the passage's arguing edge.
reasons.D: Right period diction and arguing stance, but sentences run long and flowing with fewer terse aphorisms, and it leans on borrowed tics (God save the mark) that read as imitation.
reasons.B: Plain modern expository prose: even sentence length, no period feel, no exclamations or irony, measured and neutral where the passage is tart and assertive.
